newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-minister home to face sleaze charges.
newsitem.headline: French ex-minister home to face sleaze charges.

text.p: Former French Socialist junior minister Jean-Michel Boucheron flew home on Tuesday to answer corruption charges after six years on the run in South America and was immediately arrested.

The 50-year-old politician, who was sentenced to four years in jail in his absence, came down the gangway straight into a police van on arrival at Paris' Roissy-Charles de Gaulle airport from Buenos Aires.
He gave up a long fight against a French extradition request two weeks ago and agreed to return from Argentina to face justice.

The former mayor of the southwestern town of Angouleme fled first to Uruguay in 1991 as magistrates investigated a gaping deficit in municipal finances. He went on to open a restaurant in the Argentine capital, Buenos Aires, that eventually went bankrupt.
Another French politician, ex-mayor of Nice Jacques Medecin, fled to Uruguay in the early 1990s. He was later extradited and served two years in prison prison on fraud charges.

Boucheron, convicted in his absence in 1994 of taking bribes from utility contractors, was sentenced to prison, fined and stripped of his civic rights for five years. He was held for three weeks in Argentina in 1995 and released on $50,000 bail.
"You can't live forever with a sword of Damocles above your head," he said this month, explaining his decision to return.

Boucheron was taken into custody in Bobigny near Paris until a judge decides on Friday whether he must stay in detention pending trial. Under French law, anyone sentenced in absentia is automatically entitled to a re-trial.
A former schoolteacher, Boucheron was elected mayor of Angouleme in 1977 and entered parliament the following year.

His political career collapsed soon after reaching its peak in 1988, when he was junior minister for territorial administration for just one month. An unemployed taxpayer in Angouleme first denounced suspected fraud.
Boucheron was defeated in a 1989 municipal election. Angouleme is still paying a 164-million franc ($29 million) bill for his stint as mayor.
